cases.answer: The articles do not report an FDA-validated early-stage sensitivity for EarlyCDT-Lung. The only article that discusses it is the lung liquid-biopsy review (onco-lung-liquidbiopsy.txt). Its Table 1 gives a general sensitivity range of about 13–41% (variable by setting) and specificity of about 88–91%. The table labels the test 'Investigational' and 'Commercially available in limited settings'. It does not describe the test as FDA-validated. The text says performance in other cohorts raised concerns about sensitivity for small early-stage lesions, but it gives no early-stage-specific figure. The table also does not say which stage or population the 13–41% range covers.

cases.answer: The study is a SEER-Medicare cohort of 5076 patients aged 65 or older with advanced NSCLC who received PD-1 inhibitors (1606 pembrolizumab, 3470 nivolumab). In the Fine-Gray competing-risks model, pembrolizumab was associated with significantly lower NSCLC-specific mortality than nivolumab (sHR 0.67; 95% CI 0.60-0.74; P<0.01). There was no significant difference between the two drugs for CVD mortality (sHR 1.08; 95% CI 0.63-1.84), other-cancer mortality (sHR 0.92; 95% CI 0.66-1.28) or other-disease mortality (sHR 0.71; 95% CI 0.48-1.05). The cause-specific Cox sensitivity analysis gave the same result: no significant differences for CVD, other cancers or other diseases, and lower NSCLC mortality with pembrolizumab (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.60-0.73).

claims.claim: The cohort was SEER-Medicare patients aged 65 or older with advanced NSCLC who received nivolumab or pembrolizumab.
claims.quote: aged 65 years or older with advanced NSCLC who received PD-1i (nivolumab or pembrolizumab).
